newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says U.N. civil war resolution too timid.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says U.N. civil war resolution too timid.

text.p: Zaire said on Wednesday a U.N. Security Council resolution calling for a truce in its civil war was too timid, adding that it should have condemned aggressors in the conflict.

Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda said that for Zaire, which accuses Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of invading to fight alongside rebels in the east, there could be no cessation of hostilities without a withdrawal of all foreign troops.
"This is a timid advance. We sincerely regret that this resolution does not condemn the aggressors," he told Reuters.
Tuesday's Security Council call was part of a five-point U.N. peace plan. It followed a request from U.N. special envoy Mohammed Sahnoun, who is visiting the region.

The plan envisaged an immediate ceasefire, withdrawal of all foreign forces, including mercenaries and respect for the national sovereignty and territorial integrity of Zaire and other states in the region.

Kamanda said that the resolution did not specify how the withdrawal of foreign troops would be accomplished or monitored. "If the foreign troops do not pull out, we consider that there is no cessation of hostilities," he added.
Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi reject Zaire's accusations.

The plans also called for protection of refugees and displaced persons and a peaceful settlement of the crisis through dialogue, elections and the convening of an international conference on peace, security and development.
Kamanda said the Security Council should consider Zaire's demand that it adopt a "global and unequivocal resolution on the aggression of which east Zaire is the target".
